observation_window.sampling: provider default; not continuous motion capture

extraction.teacher_style: The teacher breaks down house dance jacking into foundational movements and explains how to connect them into a flow. He uses structured verbal explanations combined with physical demonstrations to make freestyle accessible to beginners.

lesson_structure.note: Introduction to jacking style and house dance concepts
Demonstration of jacking style, footwork style, and lofting style
Explanation of house dance history and pioneers like Shannon Mabra and Tony McGregor
Introduction of four key moves: Heel Step, Farmer, Stomp, and Basic Jack
Explanation of base moves in freestyle and how to build upon them
Combining and sequencing moves like Heel Step, Stomp, and Farmer
Practicing the jacking steps to music

metaphors: the heel step is like the rhythm of my dance

steps_taught.name: Heel Step
steps_taught.description: Stepping on the heel as a base rhythm move for jacking

steps_taught.name: Farmer
steps_taught.description: A house dance move used in combination with jacking

steps_taught.name: Stomp
steps_taught.description: A grounded stomp move integrated into transitions

steps_taught.name: Basic Jack
steps_taught.description: The foundational torso and body pump movement of house dance

what_works: Categorizing house dance into distinct styles makes it easier to understand
Focusing on four core moves prevents overwhelm for beginners
what_hinders: Lack of counts makes timing relative to music harder to follow strictly

quotes.text: I like to categorize house dance into three categories.
You don't need all the moves in the book.
The heel step is kind of like the rhythm of my dance.
Doing moves means nothing unless you're doing it to music though.

extraction.distinctive_method: Categorizing house dance into three main styles (jacking, footwork, lofting) and emphasizing mastering a single 'base move' to build freestyle flow.
